image_description: A close-up, side-profile photograph of a Nile crocodile's head and upper neck. The subject is facing left, with its mouth slightly open, revealing interlocking conical teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, bony scutes on the dorsal surface and smoother scales near the jawline. The eye is visible with a reptilian appearance. The background is a soft-focus blur of dry grass and earth tones.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a distinct point, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The profile matches the taxonomic description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Teeth are clearly visible, conical, and appear to interlock. The fourth lower tooth is prominent, fitting the description of crocodilian dentition.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned high on the skull (dorsal). While the pupil shape is hard to resolve perfectly due to lighting/reflection, the placement and general reptilian structure are correct. No obvious AI distortion in the eye socket.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostril is clearly visible at the anterior tip of the snout, correctly placed for a semi-aquatic reptile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck are visible; the full body length cannot be verified from this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible neck and top of the head show distinct, rugged osteoderms/scutes with a natural, irregular but structured pattern typical of crocodile skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration is earthy grey-brown, and the texture is visibly rough and calcified, matching the ground truth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside (ventral surface) is not visible in this side-profile shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail is not visible in the frame.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species identification as Crocodylus niloticus based on snout shape and tooth arrangement.
To analyze the micro-texture of the scales for signs of AI smearing or repetitive patterns and check edge sharpness against the background.
To ensure the teeth are structurally connected to the jawbone and not floating or fused incorrectly, a common AI artifact in dental structures.

focus_areas: Tooth-jaw connectivity and individual tooth definition
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the teeth and the gum line. AI often blurs this boundary. Also, verify if the scale pattern on the neck shows any tiling or repetition artifacts which would indicate generative failure.
